blocks.zh: 第一章：導論 — 生物製藥製造設施的背景、範疇與核心概念
blocks.en: Chapter 1: Introduction — Background, Scope and Key Concepts of Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing Facilities

blocks.zh: 本章學習目標
blocks.en: Chapter Learning Objectives

blocks.zh: 理解生物製藥 (Biopharmaceutical) 與小分子藥物的本質差異，以及這些差異如何影響製造設施設計
blocks.en: Understand the fundamental differences between biopharmaceuticals and small-molecule drugs, and how these differences affect manufacturing facility design

blocks.zh: 掌握本指南的適用範圍：涵蓋哪些產品類型、對應哪些法規要求（21 CFR Part 211、EudraLex Vol.4 等）
blocks.en: Grasp the scope of this Guide: which product types it covers and which regulatory requirements it aligns with (21 CFR Part 211, EudraLex Vol.4, etc.)

blocks.zh: 深入理解六個核心概念定義：Aseptic Operation、Axenic State、Bioburden-Free、Closed System、Open System、Functionally Closed，這些定義是理解整本指南的基礎
blocks.en: Gain a thorough understanding of the six key concept definitions: Aseptic Operation, Axenic State, Bioburden-Free, Closed System, Open System and Functionally Closed. These definitions are the foundation for understanding the entire Guide

blocks.zh: 了解本指南的章節結構，能快速定位各章在整體設計決策框架中的角色
blocks.en: Understand the chapter structure of the Guide so you can quickly locate the role of each chapter within the overall design decision framework

blocks.zh: 1.1 Background 背景
blocks.en: 1.1 Background

blocks.zh: 原文內容 Original Text
blocks.en: Original Text

blocks.zh: 導師解析 Tutorial Commentary
blocks.en: Tutorial Commentary

blocks.zh: 核心概念解析 — 為何需要專屬的生物製藥設施指南？
blocks.en: Key Concept Analysis — Why Is a Dedicated Biopharmaceutical Facilities Guide Needed?

blocks.zh: 生物製藥 (Biopharmaceutical) 是指以活的細胞或生物體為基礎所生產的治療性藥物。相較於傳統化學合成的小分子藥物 (small molecule drug)，生物製藥具有以下根本差異：
blocks.en: Biopharmaceuticals are therapeutic drugs produced from living cells or organisms. Compared with traditional chemically synthesized small-molecule drugs, biopharmaceuticals differ in the following fundamental ways:

blocks.zh: 分子量極大：小分子藥物分子量通常小於 500 Da；生物製藥如單株抗體 (MAb) 分子量高達 150,000 Da — 大了 300 倍以上
blocks.en: Very large molecular weight: Small-molecule drugs typically have a molecular weight below 500 Da; a biopharmaceutical such as a monoclonal antibody (MAb) reaches about 150,000 Da, more than 300 times larger

blocks.zh: 結構複雜：具有一、二、三、四級蛋白質結構，對剪切力 (shear force)、溫度、pH 極為敏感
blocks.en: Complex structure: They have primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary protein structures that are highly sensitive to shear force, temperature and pH

blocks.zh: 由活細胞製造：製程涉及細胞培養、發酵，無法用傳統有機化學合成路徑重現
blocks.en: Manufactured by living cells: The process involves cell culture and fermentation and cannot be reproduced by conventional organic chemical synthesis routes

blocks.zh: 污染類型不同：除了化學污染外，還需面對微生物污染 (microbial contamination) 和病毒污染 (viral contamination) 的獨特挑戰
blocks.en: Different types of contamination: In addition to chemical contamination, the process faces the distinct challenges of microbial contamination and viral contamination

blocks.zh: 這些根本差異使得小分子製藥的設施設計原則無法直接套用，因此 ISPE 才編寫本專屬指南。
blocks.en: These fundamental differences mean that the facility design principles for small-molecule drugs cannot be applied directly, which is why ISPE developed this dedicated Guide.

blocks.zh: 比喻說明 — 廚房 vs. 手術室
blocks.en: Analogy — Kitchen vs. Operating Room

blocks.zh: 如果把小分子製藥比喻成「烹飪」（有明確食譜、化學反應可重現），那麼生物製藥更像是「培育一個珍稀的活體培養物」。你不只要控制溫度和食材，還要確保整個環境中沒有任何外來的微生物「闖入者」——因為一旦培養物被污染，整個批次就報廢了。這就是為什麼設施設計必須從根本上不同。
blocks.en: If small-molecule manufacturing is like "cooking" (a clear recipe, reproducible chemical reactions), then biopharmaceutical manufacturing is more like "nurturing a rare living culture." You must control not only temperature and ingredients, but also make sure no foreign microbial "intruders" enter the environment, because once the culture is contaminated, the whole batch is lost. This is why facility design has to be fundamentally different.

blocks.zh: 重點提示 — 密閉系統是本指南的核心哲學
blocks.en: Key Point — Closed Systems Are the Core Philosophy of This Guide

blocks.zh: 背景段落最後一句話極為重要：「the Guide emphasizes the use of closed systems as an approach to mitigating risks」。這不是一個建議，而是整本指南所有後續設計決策的核心哲學前提。理解「為什麼要密閉」，才能理解後面各章節中每一個設計選擇的邏輯。
blocks.en: The last sentence of the Background is extremely important: "the Guide emphasizes the use of closed systems as an approach to mitigating risks". This is not merely a recommendation; it is the core philosophical premise behind every later design decision in the Guide. Only by understanding why closure matters can you understand the logic of each design choice in the following chapters.

blocks.zh: 練習思考
blocks.en: Questions for Reflection

blocks.zh: 為什麼生物製藥生產成本遠高於傳統小分子藥物？這對設施設計有什麼影響？
blocks.en: Why is the production cost of biopharmaceuticals so much higher than that of traditional small-molecule drugs? What does this mean for facility design?

blocks.zh: 「closed systems 的實施已成為常規」這句話說明了什麼產業趨勢？這對於還在使用傳統開放式廠房的 CDMO 意味著什麼競爭壓力？
blocks.en: What industry trend does the statement "the implementation of closed systems has become routine" indicate? What competitive pressure does this create for a CDMO that still operates a traditional open facility?

blocks.zh: 1.2 Scope 適用範圍
blocks.en: 1.2 Scope

blocks.zh: 核心概念解析 — 本指南的適用對象與法規框架
blocks.en: Key Concept Analysis — Who the Guide Applies To and the Regulatory Framework

blocks.zh: 藥物原料 (Drug Substance / API) vs. 藥品 (Drug Product)：這個區別至關重要。本指南僅涵蓋 Drug Substance 的生產設施，不包含後續的充填包裝 (Fill & Finish) 作業。Fill & Finish 適用的是 EU GMP Annex 1（無菌藥品製造）等另一套規範。
blocks.en: Drug Substance (API) vs. Drug Product: This distinction is critical. This Guide covers only Drug Substance manufacturing facilities and does not cover the downstream Fill & Finish operations. Fill & Finish is governed by a different set of requirements, such as EU GMP Annex 1 (Manufacture of Sterile Medicinal Products).

blocks.zh: 適用法規的層次架構：
blocks.en: Hierarchy of applicable regulations:

blocks.zh: 美國：21 CFR Part 211（藥品 cGMP）；API 製造通常參照 ICH Q7
blocks.en: US: 21 CFR Part 211 (cGMP for drug products); API manufacturing generally follows ICH Q7

blocks.zh: 歐盟：EudraLex Vol.4 GMP Part II（API 製造要求）
blocks.en: EU: EudraLex Vol.4 GMP Part II (requirements for API manufacturing)

blocks.zh: ICH：Q7（API GMP）、Q11（化學合成 & 生技 API 開發）
blocks.en: ICH: Q7 (GMP for APIs), Q11 (development of chemical and biotechnological/biological APIs)

blocks.zh: PIC/S：Guide to GMP Part II（與 EU GMP Part II 高度一致）
blocks.en: PIC/S: Guide to GMP Part II (highly harmonized with EU GMP Part II)

blocks.zh: 產品類型一覽 — 為什麼這份清單很重要
blocks.en: Overview of Product Types — Why This List Matters

blocks.zh: 本指南涵蓋的產品類型從蛋白質到幹細胞，跨度極大。每種產品對製造環境的要求可能不同：
blocks.en: The product types covered by this Guide range widely, from proteins to stem cells. The manufacturing environment requirements may differ for each type:

blocks.zh: Monoclonal antibodies (MAbs，單株抗體)：目前生物製藥市場最大類別，哺乳類細胞培養（CHO cells）為主
blocks.en: Monoclonal antibodies (MAbs): Currently the largest category in the biopharmaceutical market, produced mainly by mammalian cell culture (CHO cells)

blocks.zh: Vaccines（疫苗）：可能需要額外的 biosafety 分級考量（活疫苗尤其嚴格）
blocks.en: Vaccines: May require additional biosafety classification considerations (live vaccines in particular are subject to stricter requirements)

blocks.zh: Gene therapy（基因治療）：新興領域，含病毒載體（AAV, lentivirus），需特殊的密閉和生物安全設計
blocks.en: Gene therapy: An emerging field involving viral vectors (AAV, lentivirus) that require special containment and biosafety design

blocks.zh: Stem cells（幹細胞）：最高複雜度，通常在小規模、高度受控環境中生產
blocks.en: Stem cells: The most complex category, usually produced at small scale in highly controlled environments

blocks.zh: 比喻說明 — 製程密閉就像密封真空包裝流水線
blocks.en: Analogy — Process Closure Is Like a Sealed Vacuum-Packing Line

blocks.zh: 想像一個生產食品的工廠。傳統的「開放式廚房」讓工人可以隨時伸手操作，但也讓空氣中的灰塵、細菌都有機會落入食品中。這就是「開放式系統 (Open System)」的概念。
blocks.en: Imagine a food factory. A traditional "open kitchen" lets workers reach in and handle food at any time, but it also gives dust and bacteria in the air a chance to fall into the food. This is the concept of an "Open System."

blocks.zh: 相較之下，現代的「密封真空包裝流水線」從食材進入到產品出廠，整個過程都在封閉管線中進行，外界環境完全無法進入。這就是「密閉系統 (Closed System)」的概念。
blocks.en: By contrast, a modern "sealed vacuum-packing line" runs the whole process, from the arrival of ingredients to the shipment of the product, inside enclosed piping, so the outside environment can never get in. This is the concept of a "Closed System."

blocks.zh: 本指南的核心訊息是：當你能讓製程「密閉」，你就可以降低周圍環境（廠房潔淨度等級）的要求——因為環境已經不是風險的主要來源了。這直接影響廠房建設成本。
blocks.en: The core message of the Guide is this: when you can make the process "closed," you can lower the requirements for the surrounding environment (cleanroom classification), because the environment is no longer the main source of risk. This directly affects facility construction cost.

blocks.zh: 重點提示 — 三個重要的「不適用」
blocks.en: Key Point — Three Important "Not Applicable" Cases

blocks.zh: 指南明確說明了三個不在範疇內的情況，這在實際工作中容易混淆：
blocks.en: The Guide clearly states three situations that fall outside its scope. These are easy to confuse in practice:

blocks.zh: 不適用於舊廠房改造評估（但如有重大修繕，可部分採用）
blocks.en: Not applicable to the assessment of existing facility retrofits (but it may be partly adopted if there is major refurbishment)

blocks.zh: 不取代 cGMP 法規（法規優先，指南是輔助合規的工具）
blocks.en: Does not replace cGMP regulations (regulations take precedence; the Guide is a tool to support compliance)

blocks.zh: 不適用於無菌藥品的充填/包裝（Fill & Finish 適用 Annex 1 等其他指南）
blocks.en: Not applicable to the filling/packaging of sterile drug products (Fill & Finish falls under Annex 1 and other guidance)

blocks.zh: 對於一個 CDMO 而言，如果你同時承接 Drug Substance 生產和 Fill & Finish，需要清楚知道哪個廠房的哪個區域應該引用哪份法規指引。
blocks.en: If a CDMO undertakes both Drug Substance manufacturing and Fill & Finish, it must be clear about which regulation or guidance applies to which area of which building.

blocks.zh: 實務應用 Practical Application
blocks.en: Practical Application

blocks.zh: 一個 CDMO 正在規劃一個新廠，客戶的管線包含 MAb（用於癌症治療）和一個新型 AAV 基因治療載體。從本章範疇，你需要注意：
blocks.en: A CDMO is planning a new facility. The client's pipeline includes a MAb (for cancer treatment) and a novel AAV gene therapy vector. From the scope of this chapter, you need to note the following:

blocks.zh: 兩者都在本指南範疇內（都是生物製藥 API）
blocks.en: Both are within the scope of this Guide (both are biopharmaceutical APIs)

blocks.zh: AAV 屬於基因治療類別，需要額外的生物安全設計考量
blocks.en: AAV falls into the gene therapy category and needs additional biosafety design considerations

blocks.zh: 如果你的工廠後面還要執行充填，那充填區需要另外引用 Annex 1 設計
blocks.en: If your facility will also perform filling, the filling area must be designed with reference to Annex 1 separately

blocks.zh: 在開始詳細設計之前，必須先諮詢主管機關（FDA/EMA）
blocks.en: Before starting detailed design, you must first consult the regulatory authorities (FDA/EMA)

blocks.zh: 本指南明確排除 Fill & Finish 作業。請思考：Drug Substance 生產的最後一個步驟（例如配方調配 formulation 或無菌過濾）和 Fill & Finish 的邊界在哪裡？這個邊界對廠房設計有什麼影響？
blocks.en: This Guide expressly excludes Fill & Finish operations. Consider: where is the boundary between the last step of Drug Substance manufacturing (for example, formulation or sterile filtration) and Fill & Finish? What effect does this boundary have on facility design?

blocks.zh: 本指南同時符合 US GMPs (21 CFR 211) 和 EU GMP (EudraLex Vol.4)。請思考：在實際設計中，如果兩者有衝突，應如何處理？
blocks.en: This Guide is aligned with both the US GMPs (21 CFR 211) and EU GMP (EudraLex Vol.4). Consider: in actual design, how should a conflict between the two be handled?

blocks.zh: 1.3 Key Concepts and Terms 核心概念與術語
blocks.en: 1.3 Key Concepts and Terms

blocks.zh: 核心概念解析 — 無菌操作 (Aseptic Operation) vs. 純淨狀態 (Axenic State)
blocks.en: Key Concept Analysis — Aseptic Operation vs. Axenic State

blocks.zh: 這兩個詞常被混淆，但有重要區別：
blocks.en: These two terms are often confused, but there is an important difference:

blocks.zh: Aseptic Operation（無菌操作）：關注的是「操作環境與物品中沒有可測到的微生物負荷」。重點在於操作過程的無菌維持——包括滅菌環境、滅菌設備、滅菌液體的搭配使用。
blocks.en: Aseptic Operation: Focuses on the absence of detectable microbial load in the operating environment and materials. The emphasis is on maintaining sterility throughout the operation, including the combined use of sterilized environments, sterilized equipment and sterilized liquids.

blocks.zh: Axenic State（純淨狀態）：專門用於細胞/微生物培養領域，指「培養物中只有目標生物體，沒有其他污染性微生物」。例如一個 CHO 細胞培養物處於 axenic state，表示裡面只有 CHO 細胞，沒有細菌、真菌等外來污染物。
blocks.en: Axenic State: Used specifically in cell and microorganism culture, it means that the culture contains only the intended organism and no other contaminating microorganisms. For example, a CHO cell culture in an axenic state contains only CHO cells, with no bacteria, fungi or other foreign contaminants.

blocks.zh: 生物製藥的上游製程（細胞培養）必須維持 axenic state；這是確保產品一致性和安全性的基礎。一旦 axenic state 被破壞（即發生「染菌 contamination」），整批細胞培養就必須報廢。
blocks.en: The upstream process of biopharmaceutical manufacturing (cell culture) must maintain an axenic state; this is the basis for product consistency and safety. Once the axenic state is lost (that is, contamination occurs), the entire cell culture batch must be discarded.

blocks.zh: 核心概念解析 — 無微生物負荷 (Bioburden-Free) vs. 低微生物負荷 (Low Bioburden)
blocks.en: Key Concept Analysis — Bioburden-Free vs. Low Bioburden

blocks.zh: 這兩個條件代表不同的嚴格程度，適用於製程的不同階段：
blocks.en: These two conditions represent different levels of stringency and apply to different stages of the process:

blocks.zh: Bioburden-Free（無微生物負荷）：完全不可偵測到任何微生物。生物反應器在使用前必須達到此狀態（滅菌）。等同於「無菌 (Sterile)」狀態。
blocks.en: Bioburden-Free: No microorganisms at all are detectable. A bioreactor must reach this state (sterilized) before use. It is equivalent to a "sterile" state.

blocks.zh: Low Bioburden（低微生物負荷）：允許有限且受控的微生物存在。例如層析純化步驟，其本質上無法完全滅菌，但透過管理措施將微生物負荷控制在可接受範圍內。
blocks.en: Low Bioburden: A limited and controlled presence of microorganisms is allowed. For example, a chromatography purification step cannot inherently be fully sterilized, but administrative and procedural controls keep the bioburden within an acceptable range.

blocks.zh: 正確區分這兩個概念對於設施設計至關重要：不同區域需要不同的環境控制等級。
blocks.en: Distinguishing these two concepts correctly is essential for facility design: different areas require different levels of environmental control.

blocks.zh: 核心概念解析 — 密閉系統 (Closed System) 與開放式系統 (Open System) 的核心差異
blocks.en: Key Concept Analysis — The Core Difference Between a Closed System and an Open System

blocks.zh: 這是整本指南最重要的概念，值得深入理解：
blocks.en: This is the most important concept in the whole Guide and deserves a thorough understanding:

blocks.zh: Closed System（密閉系統）的判斷標準：「產品永遠不暴露於周圍環境中」且「經過驗證（validated）證明污染風險已被充分控制」。關鍵在於：環境不是密閉系統的關鍵因素——這意味著密閉系統可以放在較低等級的潔淨室中，甚至是非潔淨區域。
blocks.en: Criteria for a Closed System: "the product is never exposed to the surrounding environment" and "it has been validated to demonstrate that contamination risk is adequately controlled." The key point is that the environment is not a critical factor for a closed system, which means a closed system can be placed in a lower-grade cleanroom or even in a non-classified area.

blocks.zh: Open Process（開放式製程）：產品直接暴露於環境，因此環境品質（潔淨度等級、微生物控制）成為關鍵控制因素。
blocks.en: Open Process: The product is directly exposed to the environment, so environmental quality (cleanroom classification, microbial control) becomes a critical control factor.

blocks.zh: Functionally Closed（功能性密閉）：介於兩者之間的重要概念。系統物理上可以開啟（例如 CIP/SIP 後重新使用的設備），但透過適當的清潔消毒/滅菌流程使其「等效密閉」。
blocks.en: Functionally Closed: An important concept that sits between the two. The system can physically be opened (for example, equipment that is reused after CIP/SIP), but appropriate cleaning, sanitization or sterilization procedures make it "equivalent to closed."

blocks.zh: 比喻說明 — 開放式廚房 vs. 密封真空包裝流水線
blocks.en: Analogy — Open Kitchen vs. Sealed Vacuum-Packing Line

blocks.zh: 想像兩種不同的食品加工場景：
blocks.en: Imagine two different food-processing scenarios:

blocks.zh: 開放式廚房（Open System）：廚師在開放空間中切菜、烹調，食材暴露在空氣中。為了保持食品安全，廚房必須維持高度整潔、溫濕度控制、人員衛生管理——這就像是開放式製程需要嚴格的潔淨室環境。
blocks.en: Open kitchen (Open System): Cooks cut and cook in an open space with the food exposed to the air. To keep the food safe, the kitchen must maintain a high level of tidiness, temperature and humidity control, and personnel hygiene. This is like an open process, which needs a strictly controlled cleanroom environment.

blocks.zh: 密封真空包裝流水線（Closed System）：從原料進入到成品輸出，整個過程都在封閉管線和容器中進行，沒有任何暴露點。生產車間不需要是無塵室——因為產品根本不會接觸到環境。這就是密閉系統的邏輯。
blocks.en: Sealed vacuum-packing line (Closed System): From the arrival of raw materials to the output of finished goods, the whole process takes place in enclosed piping and containers with no exposure points. The production hall does not need to be a cleanroom, because the product never touches the environment. This is the logic of a closed system.

blocks.zh: 設計決策的關鍵：密閉系統可以讓你把廠房設計在較低環境等級的空間，省下大量的潔淨室建設成本。這就是 ISPE Vol.6 指南強調「process closure」的商業邏輯所在。
blocks.en: Key to design decisions: A closed system lets you locate the facility in a space with a lower environmental grade, saving a large amount of cleanroom construction cost. This is the business logic behind the emphasis ISPE Vol.6 places on "process closure."

blocks.zh: 概念框架 — 污染風險的決定因素
blocks.en: Conceptual Framework — Determinants of Contamination Risk

blocks.zh:
污染風險 = f(製程開放程度, 環境品質, 持續時間)

密閉系統：製程開放程度 → 0
  → 環境品質的重要性降低
  → 可使用較低等級潔淨室 (CNC 或 Grade 7/8)
  → 廠房建設成本降低

開放式系統：製程開放程度 > 0
  → 環境品質成為關鍵控制點
  → 需要較高等級潔淨室 (Grade 5/6/7)
  → 廠房建設成本較高

QRM 驗證原則：
  密閉系統 → 環境不是關鍵因素 (no-impact)
  開放式系統 → 環境是關鍵因素 (direct/indirect impact)
blocks.en:
Contamination risk = f(degree of process openness, environmental quality, duration)

Closed system: degree of process openness → 0
  → environmental quality becomes less important
  → a lower-grade cleanroom can be used (CNC or Grade 7/8)
  → facility construction cost is reduced

Open system: degree of process openness > 0
  → environmental quality becomes a critical control point
  → a higher-grade cleanroom is required (Grade 5/6/7)
  → facility construction cost is higher

QRM validation principle:
  Closed system → environment is not a critical factor (no-impact)
  Open system → environment is a critical factor (direct/indirect impact)

blocks.zh: 重點提示 — CPP 和 CQA 是製程密閉策略的前提
blocks.en: Key Point — CPPs and CQAs Are the Prerequisite for a Process Closure Strategy

blocks.zh: 指南特別強調：在定義「製程密閉 (process closure)」策略之前，必須先充分理解 CPP（關鍵製程參數）和 CQA（關鍵品質屬性）。這個順序非常重要：
blocks.en: The Guide stresses that before defining a "process closure" strategy, you must first thoroughly understand the CPPs (critical process parameters) and CQAs (critical quality attributes). The sequence is very important:

blocks.zh: 首先定義 CQA — 什麼是這個產品的關鍵品質特性？
blocks.en: First define the CQAs: what are the critical quality attributes of this product?

blocks.zh: 接著識別 CPP — 哪些製程參數直接影響 CQA？
blocks.en: Then identify the CPPs: which process parameters directly affect the CQAs?

blocks.zh: 然後評估污染風險 — 環境污染如何影響 CPP 和 CQA？
blocks.en: Then assess contamination risk: how would environmental contamination affect the CPPs and CQAs?

blocks.zh: 最後決定密閉策略 — 對哪些步驟需要密閉？需要什麼等級的密閉？
blocks.en: Finally decide the closure strategy: which steps need to be closed, and what level of closure is required?

blocks.zh: 這個邏輯鏈條體現了 QbD（Quality by Design）的精髓：設計決策必須以科學理解為基礎。
blocks.en: This chain of logic embodies the essence of QbD (Quality by Design): design decisions must be based on scientific understanding.

blocks.zh: 重點提示 — Briefly Exposed 的重要性
blocks.en: Key Point — The Importance of "Briefly Exposed"

blocks.zh: 「短暫暴露 (Briefly Exposed)」是一個在實務中極為重要的中間態概念。配製緩衝液或培養基時，溶液不可避免地會短暫暴露於環境中，但隨後通過無菌過濾或熱滅菌「關閉」製程。
blocks.en: "Briefly Exposed" is an intermediate-state concept that is extremely important in practice. When buffers or media are prepared, the solution is unavoidably exposed to the environment for a short time, but the process is then "closed" by sterile filtration or heat sterilization.

blocks.zh: 關鍵設計要求：從配製到密閉的時間間隔必須被定義和驗證。這個時間窗口的長短直接影響：你需要什麼等級的製備環境（例如是否需要潔淨室），以及如何監控和驗證這個步驟。
blocks.en: Key design requirement: the time interval from preparation to closure must be defined and validated. The length of this time window directly affects what grade of preparation environment you need (for example, whether a cleanroom is required) and how this step is monitored and validated.

blocks.zh: 重要洞察：指南指出，在線（in-line）無菌過濾或熱滅菌比廠房潔淨等級更有效地控制污染風險。這是一個反直覺但重要的設計原則。
blocks.en: Important insight: the Guide states that in-line sterile filtration or heat sterilization controls contamination risk more effectively than the cleanliness grade of the facility. This is a counterintuitive but important design principle.

blocks.zh: 實務應用 — CDMO 多產品廠房的 Crossover 風險
blocks.en: Practical Application — Crossover Risk in a Multi-Product CDMO Facility

blocks.zh: 對於承接多個客戶不同產品的 CDMO，Crossover（交叉污染的一種）是重大風險。根據定義，Crossover 發生在開放式製程共享環境時，或當一個系統的密閉完整性被破壞時。
blocks.en: For a CDMO that handles different products for multiple clients, Crossover (a form of cross-contamination) is a major risk. By definition, Crossover occurs when open processes share an environment, or when the closure integrity of a system is compromised.

blocks.zh: 防止 Crossover 的設計策略：
blocks.en: Design strategies to prevent Crossover:

blocks.zh: 最佳：盡量使用密閉系統 → 物理上隔絕交叉污染的可能
blocks.en: Best: use closed systems wherever possible, physically eliminating the possibility of cross-contamination

blocks.zh: 次之：為不同產品分配獨立的潔淨室或廠房分區
blocks.en: Next best: assign separate cleanrooms or facility zones to different products

blocks.zh: 驗證：即使是密閉系統，也需驗證密閉的完整性，確保無洩漏
blocks.en: Verification: even for closed systems, the integrity of the closure must be validated to confirm there is no leakage

blocks.zh: 一個生物反應器在批次生產後，需要 CIP 清洗和 SIP 蒸汽滅菌，然後再用於下一批。這個系統屬於「Closed」、「Functionally Closed」、還是「Open」？為什麼？
blocks.en: After a production batch, a bioreactor undergoes CIP cleaning and SIP steam sterilization before it is used for the next batch. Is this system "Closed," "Functionally Closed" or "Open"? Why?

blocks.zh: 如果一個層析步驟（chromatography）在操作時需要連接管線和採樣，這使它成為「Open Process」嗎？如何才能讓它達到「Functionally Closed」的標準？
blocks.en: If a chromatography step requires connecting lines and sampling during operation, does that make it an "Open Process"? How can it be brought to the "Functionally Closed" standard?

blocks.zh: 「低微生物負荷 (Low Bioburden)」和「無菌 (Sterile)」的根本區別是什麼？在製程設計中，什麼情況下可以接受 Low Bioburden，什麼情況下必須達到 Sterile？
blocks.en: What is the fundamental difference between "Low Bioburden" and "Sterile"? In process design, when is Low Bioburden acceptable and when must Sterile be achieved?

blocks.zh: 1.4 Guide Structure 指南結構
blocks.en: 1.4 Guide Structure

blocks.zh: 核心概念解析 — 各章之間的邏輯關聯
blocks.en: Key Concept Analysis — The Logical Relationships Between Chapters

blocks.zh: 本指南的章節結構並非隨機排列，而是遵循一個由「基礎原則」到「具體設計」的邏輯層次：
blocks.en: The chapter structure of the Guide is not arbitrary; it follows a logical progression from "basic principles" to "specific design":

blocks.zh: 第1章（導論）：建立概念框架 — 為什麼需要不同的設施？核心術語是什麼？
blocks.en: Chapter 1 (Introduction): Establishes the conceptual framework — why are different facilities needed, and what are the key terms?

blocks.zh: 第2章（法規）：確立合規義務 — 必須滿足哪些要求？
blocks.en: Chapter 2 (Regulatory): Establishes compliance obligations — which requirements must be met?

blocks.zh: 第3章（風險管理）：提供決策工具 — 如何評估和量化風險？
blocks.en: Chapter 3 (Risk Management): Provides decision tools — how are risks assessed and quantified?

blocks.zh: 第4章（製程密閉）：核心設計哲學 — 如何決定哪些製程需要密閉？
blocks.en: Chapter 4 (Process Closure): The core design philosophy — how do you decide which processes need to be closed?

blocks.zh: 第5章（營運）：應用背景 — 現代生物製藥廠房如何運作？
blocks.en: Chapter 5 (Operations): The application context — how do modern biopharmaceutical facilities operate?

blocks.zh: 第6章（設施佈局）：實體設計 — 如何整合所有因素設計廠房佈局？
blocks.en: Chapter 6 (Facility Layout): Physical design — how are all the factors integrated into the facility layout?

blocks.zh: 第7-8章（建築/機電）：工程細節 — 具體的建築和設備系統如何設計？
blocks.en: Chapters 7-8 (Architectural/MEP): Engineering detail — how are the specific building and equipment systems designed?

blocks.zh: 第9章（永續性）：前瞻思維 — 如何兼顧環保要求？
blocks.en: Chapter 9 (Sustainability): Forward-looking thinking — how are environmental requirements balanced?

blocks.zh: 比喻說明 — 建造一棟生物製藥廠就像蓋一棟醫院
blocks.en: Analogy — Building a Biopharmaceutical Plant Is Like Building a Hospital

blocks.zh: 你不會在不了解病患需求（CQA）和醫療流程（製程）的情況下開始設計醫院的建築平面圖。你需要先知道：要服務什麼類型的病人？有哪些感染控制要求？如何讓潔淨區和污染區分流？本指南的章節順序就是這個「從需求到設計」的邏輯流程。
blocks.en: You would not start designing a hospital floor plan without understanding patient needs (CQAs) and clinical workflows (the process). You first need to know what type of patients will be served, what infection control requirements apply, and how to separate clean and contaminated flows. The chapter order of this Guide follows the same "from requirements to design" logic.

blocks.zh: 重點提示 — 第3章和第4章是核心
blocks.en: Key Point — Chapters 3 and 4 Are the Core

blocks.zh: 對於設施設計工程師和品質人員來說，第3章（風險管理）和第4章（製程密閉）是最重要的兩章。它們回答了最關鍵的問題：
blocks.en: For facility design engineers and quality professionals, Chapter 3 (Risk Management) and Chapter 4 (Process Closure) are the two most important chapters. They answer the most critical questions:

blocks.zh: 第3章：如何系統性地評估污染風險？（工具：FMEA、HAZOP、HACCP、ICH Q9）
blocks.en: Chapter 3: How do you systematically assess contamination risk? (Tools: FMEA, HAZOP, HACCP, ICH Q9)

blocks.zh: 第4章：基於風險評估結果，如何決定哪些步驟需要密閉，以及對應的環境分級？
blocks.en: Chapter 4: Based on the risk assessment results, how do you decide which steps need to be closed, and what are the corresponding environmental classifications?

blocks.zh: 這兩章的結論直接決定了你的廠房需要多少 ISO 5/6/7/8 潔淨室，從而直接影響廠房建設成本。
blocks.en: The conclusions of these two chapters directly determine how much ISO 5/6/7/8 cleanroom space your facility needs, and therefore directly affect facility construction cost.

blocks.zh: 重點提示 — 第5章提到的趨勢對 CDMO 的意義
blocks.en: Key Point — What the Trends in Chapter 5 Mean for a CDMO

blocks.zh: 第5章提到幾個重要的產業趨勢：
blocks.en: Chapter 5 describes several important industry trends:

blocks.zh: 多產品設施 (Multi-product facilities)：為了降低成本，越來越多工廠需要在同一設施中生產多個不同客戶的產品，這對於防止交叉污染的設計要求極高
blocks.en: Multi-product facilities: To reduce cost, more and more plants need to manufacture different clients' products in the same facility, which places very high demands on cross-contamination prevention design

blocks.zh: 更高的效價 (Higher titers)：製程改進使得每批可以生產更多產品，意味著可以用更小規模的設施服務更多患者
blocks.en: Higher titers: Process improvements allow more product to be made per batch, which means a smaller facility can serve more patients

blocks.zh: 一次性使用技術 (Single-use technology)：有助於降低交叉污染風險、減少清潔驗證工作量
blocks.en: Single-use technology: Helps reduce cross-contamination risk and the cleaning validation workload

blocks.zh: 實務應用 — 如何使用本指南作為決策工具
blocks.en: Practical Application — How to Use This Guide as a Decision Tool

blocks.zh: 在實際的廠房設計項目中，建議按以下流程使用本指南：
blocks.en: In an actual facility design project, we recommend using the Guide in the following sequence:

blocks.zh: 第1章：確認你的產品類型是否在範疇內
blocks.en: Chapter 1: Confirm whether your product type is within scope

blocks.zh: 第2章：識別適用的法規要求（哪個市場？FDA/EMA？）
blocks.en: Chapter 2: Identify the applicable regulatory requirements (which market? FDA/EMA?)

blocks.zh: 第3章：選擇適當的風險評估方法（FMEA/HAZOP/HACCP）
blocks.en: Chapter 3: Select an appropriate risk assessment method (FMEA/HAZOP/HACCP)

blocks.zh: 第4章：基於風險評估決定哪些製程需要密閉，決定環境分級
blocks.en: Chapter 4: Based on the risk assessment, decide which processes need to be closed and determine the environmental classifications

blocks.zh: 第6章：根據製程密閉策略設計廠房佈局和流向
blocks.en: Chapter 6: Design the facility layout and flows according to the process closure strategy

blocks.zh: 第7-8章：具體建築和機電設計
blocks.en: Chapters 7-8: Detailed architectural and MEP design

blocks.zh: 如果一個 CDMO 同時有早期臨床（Phase 1/2）和商業化生產的業務，指南第5章提到的「產品聚焦患者群體」這個趨勢意味著什麼？對工廠設計有什麼彈性要求？
blocks.en: If a CDMO has both early clinical (Phase 1/2) and commercial manufacturing business, what does the trend of "product-focused patient populations" mentioned in Chapter 5 of the Guide imply? What flexibility does it require of the facility design?

blocks.zh: 第9章談到永續性（LEED、BREEAM）。在生物製藥廠房設計中，潔淨室的能耗極高（大量的空調換氣）。製程密閉策略如何幫助降低能耗，同時符合永續性目標？
blocks.en: Chapter 9 discusses sustainability (LEED, BREEAM). In biopharmaceutical facility design, cleanrooms consume a great deal of energy (large volumes of HVAC air changes). How can a process closure strategy help reduce energy consumption while meeting sustainability goals?

blocks.zh: 本章重點回顧 Chapter Summary
blocks.en: Chapter Summary

blocks.zh: 生物製藥的本質差異決定了設施設計必須採用不同的原則：活體細胞製造、分子量大、對污染高度敏感，需要比傳統小分子藥物更嚴格的製程控制
blocks.en: The fundamental differences of biopharmaceuticals mean that facility design must follow different principles: manufacture by living cells, large molecular size and high sensitivity to contamination require tighter process control than traditional small-molecule drugs

blocks.zh: 製程密閉 (Process Closure) 是本指南的核心哲學：密閉系統可以降低對周圍環境的依賴，從而在不犧牲產品品質的前提下降低廠房建設和運營成本
blocks.en: Process closure is the core philosophy of this Guide: Closed systems reduce reliance on the surrounding environment, lowering facility construction and operating costs without sacrificing product quality

blocks.zh: 六個核心術語構成理解全書的基礎：Aseptic Operation（無菌操作）、Axenic State（純淨狀態）、Bioburden-Free（無微生物負荷）、Closed System（密閉系統）、Functionally Closed（功能性密閉）、Open Process（開放式製程）
blocks.en: Six key terms form the basis for understanding the whole Guide: Aseptic Operation, Axenic State, Bioburden-Free, Closed System, Functionally Closed and Open Process

blocks.zh: 本指南適用於 Drug Substance 的生產設施，不適用於 Fill & Finish（充填包裝）；同時兼顧 21 CFR Part 211（US）和 EudraLex Vol.4 GMP Part II（EU）等主要法規
blocks.en: This Guide applies to Drug Substance manufacturing facilities and not to Fill & Finish; it is aligned with the major regulations, including 21 CFR Part 211 (US) and EudraLex Vol.4 GMP Part II (EU)

blocks.zh: CPP 和 CQA 的理解是製程密閉決策的前提：必須先知道什麼對產品品質最重要，才能科學地決定哪些製程環節需要密閉保護
blocks.en: Understanding CPPs and CQAs is the prerequisite for process closure decisions: you must first know what matters most to product quality before you can scientifically decide which process steps need closure protection

blocks.zh: 指南章節遵循邏輯層次：從法規基礎→風險評估工具→製程密閉策略→設施佈局→工程細節，每一層建立在前一層的基礎上
blocks.en: The chapters follow a logical hierarchy: from regulatory foundation → risk assessment tools → process closure strategy → facility layout → engineering detail, with each layer building on the one before
